If someone misses an appointment, first check the time, transport, interpreter and work schedule. Confirm the plan in the language the person uses, and ask whether it works for them.

Book a qualified interpreter instead of using a child to go between.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Vietnamese is tonal, and the Northern, Central, and Southern varieties are not always interchangeable in an interpreter, so put the variety on the line if it matters in this room. Still book a qualified interpreter, because a list is not the person and not the dialect, and CLAS still stands.

### Language

Compass reports that among those 5 and older, about 66.9 percent speak a language other than English and about 35.5 percent speak English less than “very well,” and you should date the number. Many elders read quốc ngữ while some do not, and second-generation English is common, but the IEP still has to reach the parent.

Give the person time to answer. If you get a short yes, check that the plan was understood, and ask whether it works for them.

Do not use a child as the interpreter, and do not make a Vietnamese coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
sections.body:
This section states hard facts plainly, because treating everyone the same can hide them.

### Named harms

Boat-people trauma is real in some rooms — the sea, the camps, the loss — but it is not a personality, and it is not a reason to skip screening; it is a reason a government badge is not automatically help.

Intra-community 1975 politics still split some rooms — first wave and later arrivals, the flag, April 30 — so you do not referee, and you do not put it on a case note as color.

Gambling is a named harm in some families, but it is not a race trait, so you follow the law and you still see a family.

Nail-salon labor is work, not a personality and not a joke, and chemicals, hours, and pay are labor facts, so do not write “nails” as ethnicity.

Deportation of Vietnamese people with certain convictions — including people who have lived here since childhood — is current structure, not folklore, and it changes who opens the door. Do not collect status you do not need, and do not treat fear as noncompliance.

LGBTQ Vietnamese Minnesotans exist, so you use the name, and you do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Staff who share this community may add facts, but they do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Believe reported pain, and do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic Asian slide, because this is not the Hmong page and not the Chinese page.

### Access

Hepatitis B screening for people born in Vietnam is a U.S. public-health pattern; CDC has treated Vietnam as a higher-prevalence birth country in its screening guidance. Date the CDC page you cite, do not invent a Minnesota rate, and do not skip screening because the person looks well.

Mental-health stigma is real in some families, and war trauma, depression, and somatic presentation exist. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one, and a smile is not a PHQ-9.

Traditional medicine — thuốc nam, coining, cupping, herbs — often sits beside biomedicine, so ask and work it out together. Do not mock marks on skin as abuse by default, and do not skip a child-protection duty when the facts are the facts. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care, so offer it.

Late help-seeking can be language, stigma, and a lobby that already used a child as the interpreter, which is one more reason not to skip screening.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Vietnamese Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, temple, and parish climates can mean silence or exile, and some people live a public English life and a private Vietnamese life, which is why you use the name they use and do not share what they tell you unless a rule requires it.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. Use the name the person uses, and do not share what they tell you unless a rule requires it. Do not question a household about anyone’s sexuality or gender, and take seriously that some people have reason to keep it private.

Do not let concern about family reputation or 1975 politics override what this person wants, and always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Áo dài is public at Tết, weddings, and some school or parish stages, but it is not a daily uniform, and the second generation looks like Minnesota, so do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

For hair and head, follow this person, and do not touch. Gold, a Buddhist bracelet, a cross, or a wedding huế is not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

Nail-salon work may mean stained hands and chemical exposure, which is labor, not a joke and not a race trait.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Cải lương, nhạc vàng, diaspora pop, karaoke as social life in some rooms, Buddhist chant, and Catholic hymn are all here, and a New Year stage may hold more than one of them, which is named variation rather than a playlist.

### Variation

A funeral is not staff entertainment, and a playlist is not engagement. Knowing that 1975 politics can sit inside a song will stop you from putting the wrong flag on a speaker.

Tết stages are public life, but they are not consultation and not a case plan.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Soccer and badminton show up in public Vietnamese Minnesota life, and school sport is ordinary for the second generation, but do not assume the kid plays, and do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

### Not the whole person

Sport clubs are social infrastructure for some, but they are not language access and not a case plan, and Greater Minnesota teams are still this people.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Quốc ngữ made a modern written public, and oral forms, poetry, and diaspora memoir sit beside it. Minnesota and U.S. Vietnamese writers, journalists, and scholars exist, though you do not need to quote a novel in the lobby.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do need to know this is not a people without letters, and while many elders read Vietnamese, some do not. A notice that exists only in English will not work, and a notice in Vietnamese the elder cannot read also will not work, so ask.

Tones and diacritics are not decoration, because a name stripped of its marks on a form can still be the wrong person, so write what they tell you.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Calligraphy, temple sculpture and painting, diaspora visual work, and the public culture of markets and Tết are all part of this people’s art, while phở and bánh mì are a foodway, not consultation.

### Guest

You are a guest rather than a researcher, and a market visit is not a case plan. A museum or temple visit is optional professional development rather than consultation, and you should not photograph an altar.

A Heritage Month that mashes this people with Hmong paj ntaub or a Chinese New Year poster has already mashed the adjacent peoples.

sections.heading: War, the State, and Deportation Climate
sections.body:
The American War / Vietnam War, 30 April 1975, the boats, the camps, Orderly Departure, and a United States that fought, left, and then resettled — that is the political event. Later came policing and the deportation of people with records, including people who have lived here since childhood, which is why a DHS badge is not automatically help.

### The badge

Do not use 1975 as a personality, and do not ask a veteran or a boat-person to narrate dying for your professional development. Intra-community politics about the flag and April 30 are real, and you do not referee them on a case note.

The deportation climate changes who opens the door, who signs, and who will not put a relative’s name on a form, and that is not noncompliance, so do not collect status you do not need.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
sections.body:
Work here spans the shop, the restaurant, the factory, a professional second generation, and public employment. Nail-salon labor is a documented Vietnamese American work pattern, but it is work; it is not a personality, not a joke, and not the whole economy. Chemicals and hours are labor facts, so do not write “nails” as ethnicity.

### Work

Markets and University Avenue commerce are both economy and culture, but a food-court visit is not consultation.

### Staff

Book a qualified interpreter, and pay for community work. Do not assign either to staff because of who they are.

Take time to introduce yourself and explain the plan, and still give any required notice.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Several things arrive together in these encounters: language and variety, family-name order, who is in the room, a child pushed forward as the English speaker, an altar or a priest or a monk in the story, pain you must believe, the deportation climate, and a nuclear form that reversed the name.

### Language

Confirm the variety if it matters, and still book a qualified interpreter rather than using a child. Offer gender match, ask who should hear, and ask which name is the family name, and do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

If they name traditional medicine, listen, while remembering that mandated reporting still exists. Believe reported pain.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
This people is not Hmong, not Lao, not Cambodian, not Chinese, and not Korean, and “Asian American” is not the file, so open the Hmong CI for Hmong and open this one for Vietnamese. Some households are mixed, and Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) are in some families, so ask this household. Do not file them under Chinese by default, and do not deny it if they name it.

### Adjacent doors

A shared war in Southeast Asia is not shared culture. Camps in Thailand are a Hmong story and other peoples’ story as well, so do not mash the camp into one Asian refugee, and remember that Karen is a different spine.

Never one Asian module, and never one “Southeast Asian” interpreter.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass (ACS 2020–2024) describes the Vietnamese cultural community this way. The count is about 32,841 (give or take 3,477), with 76.8% in the Twin Cities and 23.2% in Greater Minnesota, and about 27.4% are age 17 or younger and 8.4% are 65+. Foreign-born is 48.5%, and among those age 5 and older, 66.9% speak a language other than English and 35.5% speak English less than “very well.” Among those 25 and older, 77.0% have high school or higher and 36.1% have a bachelor’s or higher. Median household income is about $92,644 (give or take $9,598, in 2024 dollars), poverty is 10.5%, owner-occupied housing is 70.1%, and average household size is 2.95. Compass also shows 8.4% (give or take 1.8) with a disability and 6.0% (give or take 1.5) of those under 65; the State Demographic Center counts about 1,000 (give or take 500) adults ages 18 to 64 with a disability. These figures are survey estimates with wide margins.

### Counts

Date Compass, and do not invent other rates. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions (ancestry vs. birthplace vs. language), so date the number you cite.

### What the count is not

A young age structure is not a personality, and an owner rate is not proof the gates closed. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates, and a rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
Start with the Minnesota Compass Vietnamese profile (ACS 2020–2024). Then turn to the DHS Equal Opportunity and Access LEP resources, where Vietnamese appears on the five, on the ten-language block, and on the fifteen interpreter cards, while remembering that a list is not the notice and not the interpreter.

### Public doors

The Vietnamese Community of Minnesota, and the Buddhist temples and Catholic parishes that families name, are public doors, and CECLC is a door, not the whole community.

### Where to learn more

Use these resources yourself before you ask a Vietnamese colleague to explain, and do not count a BCC to a temple or a parish as consultation. Pay partners and report back, and be a guest at Tết if invited, knowing that it is not consultation.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates here.

Language comes first: an interpreter labeled Vietnamese who does not speak this household’s variety will not work, but you still book a qualified interpreter, because a list is not the person and not the dialect, and you do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names come next: the family name is first in Vietnamese order, and the database that reverses Nguyễn without asking invents a person, so do not joke about Nguyễn.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

In child welfare and disability, help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists, and so does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score.

On deportation climate, people may skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved, and that is not noncompliance, so do not collect status you do not need.

On notices and comment, do not count an eList and an English PDF as reaching this community, and record who was reached and what follow-up happened. Greater Minnesota is 23.2 percent, so a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

On workforce, Vietnamese staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community; staff are colleagues, not the curriculum, and you do not treat them as either.

On the Asian mash, opening Hmong or Karen or Chinese because the checkbox says Asian shuts the person out.

On legislation, funding, and rule, study a channel before you advocate for it. Use this page so that the 40% has a household in it.

sections.heading: 0. How to use this — who this is, who this is not
sections.body:
This door sits on the spine because every Compass cultural community in Minnesota gets covered, wide and deep, with no one left over. Keep in mind that a Compass count is not government-to-government, so for questions of sovereignty you should open the Eleven Nations CI. Urban Native is not off the list.

Counts disagree across ACS vintages, which is why you should date whatever you cite. Compass uses IPUMS ACS 2020–2024, and people who belong to more than one group can appear in more than one Compass profile.

A few boundaries hold throughout: this is not a racial module, it is not a Tribal Nation unless the household is, and it is not permission to skip language access or the Toolkit.

sections.heading: 1. Origins
sections.body: Full origin chapters will grow to African American depth as we write them, and nothing here is lite simply because the count is smaller. The pattern comes now, the ethnography comes next, and all of it stays unvarnished.

sections.heading: 2. Geography — Minnesota, dated
sections.body: You can open the live, dated Compass table here: https://www.mncompass.org/topics/demographics/cultural-communities/native-american

sections.heading: 4. Minnesota specifically
sections.body: Arrive as a guest, pay, and report back afterward, because an eList is not engagement.

sections.heading: 5. Core concepts
sections.body: The Compass count is not government-to-government, so for sovereignty you should open the Eleven Nations CI, remembering that Urban Native is not off the list. That is the first grammar to learn here, while the rest is written at full depth rather than guessed at to look complete.

sections.heading: 7. Language, names, communication
sections.body: An interpreter who is labeled only with a country name can still be speaking the wrong language.

sections.heading: 9. Other considerations — unvarnished
sections.body: ERGs are welcome to add, but they may not delete a fact simply because it is hard to say in a Minimization room.

sections.heading: 15. How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body: An identical process is Minimization, which is why the pattern here is a universal goal with a targeted channel. This door exists so that the packet has a household in it.

sections.heading: 16. What you will not conclude
sections.body: If you leave saying that you know this people now, the intelligence has failed, since it has become a capsule.
